title: Introduce pluggable decision adapters and regional circuit-breakers in smart routing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: The current smart routing stack mixes policy evaluation, fallback ranking, and regional overload protection in a single monolithic hotpath. This has caused high lock contention and makes it difficult to iterate on fallback heuristics without risking latency regressions. Goals: 1) Split the routing hotpath into clear pluggable adapters (policy evaluator, capacity scorer, fallback sorter). 2) Add regional circuit-breakers with token-bucket-based admission and exponential backoff on overload. 3) Reduce global lock contention by introducing per-shard read paths and an immutable decision cache for short-lived requests. 4) Keep API compatibility and allow gradual rollout per region/customer tier. Non-goals: Rewriting the serving runtime or changing model selection heuristics in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Routing hotpath split into at least three adapters with documented interfaces and unit tests
End-to-end P50 latency for 1k concurrent small requests does not regress >5% on benchmark cluster
Global lock contention on routing mutex reduced by at least 70% in flame graphs
Regional circuit-breaker engages under synthetic overload and gracefully routes to fallback variants
Can enable/disable new routing adapters via feature flag and rollout by region
Migration plan and rollback documented in design doc and confluence
Automated integration tests cover adapter contract and fallback behavior
plan: Design review and finalize adapter interfaces (policy, capacity, fallback) - deliverable: design doc and interface protos
Prototype locally: extract current evaluator into adapter shim to validate invariants
Implement regional circuit-breaker module with metrics and admin controls
Replace monolithic hotpath with adapter dispatcher, add per-shard read copy for routing state
Run performance regression suite and flamegraph before/after
Split changes into two PRs: core adapter interfaces + compatibility shim, then adapter implementations and circuit-breakers
Canary rollout to staging regions, observe telemetry for 72 hours, then gradual rollout to production regions
migration_steps: Deploy PR-1 (adapter interfaces + shims) behind feature flag to staging
Run integration tests and synthetic load benchmarks against staging cluster
Deploy PR-2 (adapters + circuit-breaker) to canary region with feature flag enabled for 10% traffic
Monitor metrics: latency, errors, breaker firing rate, routing cache hit ratio
If stable for 72 hours, increase traffic to 50% then 100% in region-by-region phases
If regression observed, flip feature flag off for affected region and roll back PR-2
testing: Unit tests for adapter interfaces and fallback sorter
Integration tests exercising regional overload and verifying circuit-breaker behavior
Load tests replicating 95th/99th percentile path workloads used by client teams
Chaos test: simulate transient region capacity drop and verify safe fallback promotion
Observation smoke tests: ensure tracing and metrics propagate through adapters
comments: 2026-02-18 - Ava Chen: Triage note - flagged as P1 tech-debt; routing hotpath frequently shows high mutex wait in production flamegraphs. Suggested splitting responsibilities to reduce contention and make fallbacks pluggable.
2026-02-25 - Priya Singh: Design review - asked for clearer adapter contracts and compatibility with existing trace/span headers. Also requested admin metrics for circuit-breaker thresholds.

2026-03-01 - Miguel Torres: Prototype update - extracted evaluator into adapter shim; local benchmarks show 40% reduction in mutex hold time but a ~3% increase in P50 due to adapter dispatch overhead. Plan to micro-optimize dispatch and add inline fast-path for common cases.

2026-03-05 - Omar Haddad: Bench results posted - after inlining fast-path and caching decision objects, benchmark P50 restored and P95 improved by ~6% on synthetic key-prefix-heavy workload. Flamegraphs show per-shard reads eliminated global serialization.

2026-03-09 - Design review feedback - Security requested review of metrics exposure for circuit-breakers; added admin-only Prometheus labels and RBAC gating for manual breaker overrides. Documented in https://go.redwood/confluence/routing/circuit-breaker-admin

2026-03-11 - Code review - PR-1 approved with minor naming comments (resolved). Split PR-2 to isolate protocol buffer upgrade to reduce risk; noted dependency bump: google.golang.org/grpc -> v1.60.0 and github.com/prometheus/client_golang -> v1.16.0.
